selected.title: Google Genie 4: Change the Weather in a World You Can Walk Through
selected.summary: Google began a November 18 rollout of Genie 4 in browser-based Project Genie for eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers. A text prompt can steer the world while the person is navigating, and native sound adapts as the scene changes.
selected.availability: Rolling out to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers aged 18+. Google AI Pro members can join the waitlist.
selected.practical_use: Create an imagined street and try one weather change while exploring.

source_review.excerpt: you can now prompt mid-session to change the world you created
source_review.decision: Read the November 18 rollout, the earlier trusted-tester announcement, Project Genie setup and model card. The example is illustrative.
source_review.availability: Rolling out to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers aged 18+. Google AI Pro members can join the waitlist.

openai.reason: GPT‑6.2 Astra in ChatGPT Work: Build an Excel Report You Can Check is reserved for its separate professional episode.

anthropic.reason: November 17 Linked Billing is a documented beta for API customers, with narrower relevance. The recent IPO does not change a Claude workflow. November 9 Fable 5.2 / Mythos 5.2 is outside the Daily window.

google.reason: Genie 4 now reaches eligible consumers with an unusually tangible interaction. Gemini 4 Neon is a separate November 18 flagship launch deferred for a specific workflow rather than a benchmark roundup.

repositories.reason: LocalAI 5.0: Turn a Folder of Notes Into a Word File on Your Own Server is reserved for its separate repositories episode.

architectures.reason: Genie 4 model card documents its transformer basis and multimodal inputs. Use it to verify the consumer story's limits and keep implementation detail out of the episode.

playlist_review.reason: The entire episode answers the everyday viewer's question and stays within the everyday playlist. The weather change makes the new interaction easy to picture and demonstrates the difference between exploring a generated scene and directing it as it unfolds.

editorial_review.viewer_question: Can I change a world while I'm walking around inside it?
editorial_review.prerequisites: An eligible adult Google AI Ultra account in a supported region and a web browser.
editorial_review.central_task: Create an imagined street and try one weather change while exploring.
editorial_review.new_capability: Consumer rollout on November 18 after October 27 trusted-tester preview, with documented mid-session steering and adaptive native audio in Genie 4.
editorial_review.closest_archive_coverage: October 7 covered wide image edits with Nano Banana, a different tool and task. The archive has no Project Genie episode.
editorial_review.supported_payoff: Walk down a sunny street, then ask Genie 4 to turn it into a snowy evening while you explore.
editorial_review.evidence_mode_reason: Illustrative prompt based on Google's documented controls.
editorial_review.alternatives: Separate releases from the other providers were reviewed for their own audiences.
editorial_review.selection_rationale: The weather change makes the new interaction easy to picture and demonstrates the difference between exploring a generated scene and directing it as it unfolds.
editorial_review.search_query: Google Genie 4: Change the Weather in a World You Can Walk Through
editorial_review.availability_limitation: Experimental preview. Scene details can drift over time. We reviewed Google's documentation and did not run Genie 4.
editorial_review.final_verdict: The opening, walkthrough and closing all deliver one concrete task. The weather change makes the new interaction easy to picture and demonstrates the difference between exploring a generated scene and directing it as it unfolds.
editorial_review.metadata_review: Title identifies tool and task. Thumbnail expresses the outcome in a short phrase. Description discloses the date, access and evidence limits.
